title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 34–36). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'réseau': a poset M of pieces (think of a lattice of tame or semi-algebraic subsets, or of the members of a 'découpage'). In M the operations ∧ and ∨ and the complement X ↦ X' are well behaved only on families in 'modular' (also called 'médiant') position. M also carries a class M_f of closed elements and a closure X ↦ X̄. Axioms 1)–7) are stated on earlier pages. On p.34 he relativizes to an element A, setting M_A = M_{≤A} = {Y ∈ M : Y ⊂ A}. He then begins checking that M_A again satisfies 1)–7). The relative complement is X ↦ X' ∧ A, characterized as the largest Y ⊂ A in modular position with X and disjoint from it. The closed elements of M_A are the Z ∧ A with Z ∈ M_f and {Z, A} modular.

This page finishes axiom 4 and handles 5 and 6.

(Axiom 4, Boolean generation.) Take X_i ∈ M_A mutually modular, i.e. X_i ⊂ A, mutually modular and modular with A. Generate with the operations of M_A: ∁_{M_A} (unary), ∧, ∨ (binary), and the constants 0_{M_A}, 1_{M_A} = A. He claims this gives the same thing as generating in M with ∁_M, ∧, ∨, 0_M, 1_M and then 'multiplying by A', i.e. applying b ↦ b ∧ A. So what one finds is the image of a Boolean algebra under b ↦ b ∧ A. That image is the relative algebra B|A, a Boolean algebra with complement b ↦ b' ∧ A; hence 'c'est une alg. de Boole'.

The key compatibility step: {X, Y} modular in M_A implies {∁_{M_A}X, ∁_{M_A}Y} modular. Proof: in M, {X', Y'} is modular, and X', Y' are also modular with A (all lie in the Boolean algebra generated by X, Y, A). Hence {A ∧ X', A ∧ Y'} is modular. OK.

(Axiom 5) Trivial.

(Axiom 6, closure.) For X ⊂ A, the closed elements of M_A containing X are the Y ∧ A with Y ∈ M_f, {Y, A} modular and Y ⊃ X. Since Y is closed, Y ⊃ X is equivalent to Y ⊃ X̄. The smallest such is obtained for Y = X̄, so the closure in M_A is X̄^M ∧ A (completed on p.36). This is the lattice-theoretic form of 'closure in a subspace = ambient closure ∩ subspace'.

Purpose: show the class of réseaux is stable under passage to a 'subspace' A. This is preparatory to defining connectedness and components (p.36), via clopen elements forming a Boolean algebra.
errors: The Boolean-generation claim (generate in M, then multiply by A) is asserted ('on croit que'), not proved. It needs the X_i together with A to be mutually modular in M, and needs b ↦ b ∧ A to be a homomorphism onto the relative algebra; that holds inside a Boolean algebra but relies on the earlier axioms.
In the closure argument (6), he must also check that X̄ is modular with A, so that X̄ ∧ A is a legitimate closed element of M_A. This is tacit here.
On p.34 (previous page) 1_{M_A} = X is a slip for 1_{M_A} = A.

ideas.what: Relativization of a réseau/découpage structure to the down-set M_{≤A}, with relative complement X' ∧ A
ideas.modern_name: Interval/relative algebra [0,A] (relative Boolean algebra; in orthomodular lattices, [0,a] with x ↦ x' ∧ a)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lattice theory (Birkhoff; for orthomodular lattices Kalmbach and others)

ideas.what: Mutually 'modular' families generate a Boolean algebra; relativized generation equals ambient generation followed by meet with A
ideas.modern_name: Compatible elements generating Boolean subalgebras (partial Boolean algebras / orthomodular lattices)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kochen–Specker (partial Boolean algebras, 1960s); Foulis, Holland and others (orthomodular lattices)

ideas.what: Closure in the relative structure equals ambient closure meet A
Overall program: a point-free, lattice-axiomatic 'tame topology' via découpages, with partially defined Boolean operations
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology / o-minimal-style axiomatics in point-free form
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight; Grothendieck's call for tame topology: Esquisse d'un programme §5
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tame topology programmatically, not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'mutually modular/médiant' families, which generate genuine Boolean algebras inside a structure that is only partially Boolean, behave like compatible families in orthomodular lattices or Kochen–Specker partial Boolean algebras. His relative complement X' ∧ A on M_{≤A} is the standard orthomodular relativization. As far as I know the link between these unpublished tame-topology lattice axiomatics and quantum-logic lattice theory has not been noted.
missed.quote: on croit que c'est pareil que des premières ∁_M, ∧, ∨, 0_M, 1_M — et de multiplier par A ... c'est une alg. de Boole
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could let Grothendieck's réseau axioms be compared with, or reduced to, known structure theory (orthomodular lattices, partial Boolean algebras, effect algebras). That would help any modern reconstruction of his point-free tame topology. The interest is modest: the page itself is routine verification.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine verification that axioms survive relativization to a sub-object (relative Boolean algebra, subspace closure). The only interest is the broader unpublished program of lattice-axiomatic tame topology and its unremarked resemblance to partial Boolean algebra / orthomodular structures.
transcription_corrections: 'des X_i ⊂ A mut. mod et mod p.r. à A contenu[?])' is likely '(i.e. des X_i ⊂ A mut. mod. et mod. p.r. à A ...)', the X_i being modular with A as well.
'et des recoller[?] multiplier[?] par A' reads as 'et de multiplier par A' (i.e. take ∧ A).

'Donc on croit que l'on trouve ici l'idée d'une alg. de Boole' is plausibly 'Donc on voit que l'on trouve ici l'image d'une alg. de Boole' (the image under ∧A), consistent with 'c'est une alg. de Boole'.
'Je pense prouver que' is plausibly 'Il faut prouver que'.
The struck line 'les op. ∁_A, ∧, ∨ (binaires)' is replaced by '∁_{M_A} (unaires), ∧, ∨ (binaires)'.
The marginal superscripts 'X', 'Y' near 'comme' / 'donc' indicate X', Y' (the complements), i.e. 'comme X', Y' sont mod. avec A'.
Page 34: '1_{M_A} = X' should read '1_{M_A} = A'; and 'connexe [?]' there is probably 'modulaire'/'médiant'.
